original.reason: It only discusses the special case with two equal variables, relies on unspecified numerical evaluation, and makes an unsupported leap from symmetry/boundary behavior to the general three-variable result.

judgment.reason: The asserted pairwise factorization of equality of logarithmic derivatives is false: the derivative ratio is not injective on positive reals. Boundary liminf and existence claims are also asserted without proof.
Its auxiliary lemma is the original claim, and its purported proof relies on the same false pairwise factorization and unproved boundary-minimum assertions.
The critical-point argument incorrectly concludes equality of variables from a false factorization; its boundary and compactness/minimum assertions are not justified.
Although h(x)≥3x is correct, it yields product h(ai)≥27abc, while AM–GM gives 27abc≤(a+b+c)^3, the opposite direction needed for the claimed conclusion.
